review_note: Keep the repair and apology demonstrations, brief satire and explicit correction. Align frequency wording with week 4, identify the cost table as a proposal, and remove predicted student errors and self-congratulation from notes.

edits.before: description: "The week 5 lecture deck: repair as steady-state traffic, the three initiators, “huh?” as a word, and an apology template the evidence made this course correct."
edits.after: description: "The week 5 lecture deck: repair as steady-state traffic, the three initiators, “huh?” as a word, and the corrected apology template."
edits.reason: Describe the deck without advertising the course's willingness to correct itself before the correction is shown.

edits.before: - This is the reframe the week turns on. Let it sit before moving to the table.
edits.after: - Pause before moving to the table.
edits.reason: Keep the delivery cue and remove the repeated declaration of a turning point.

edits.before: Repairs faster than "what?", and shows the speaker exactly which part you caught.
edits.after: Shows the speaker exactly which part you caught.
edits.reason: Match the revised lecture: the example identifies the trouble, while the study measures time to initiate repair rather than total repair duration.

edits.before: - This is the week's first sincere instruction and the one to actually practise.
edits.after: - Have students say the example aloud.
edits.reason: Replace a claim of sincerity with the practice it introduces.

edits.before: ## And "faster" is literal
edits.after: ## When repair begins
edits.reason: Name the quantity measured in the following study without repeating the removed faster-repair claim.

edits.before: Most repair initiations came after gaps of about **700 ms**.
edits.after: The most frequent gap before a repair initiation was about **700 ms**.
edits.reason: Match the lecture and week 4's record of a most-frequent interval, rather than asserting that most cases shared it.

edits.before: - So if "sorry, what?" makes you wince, you're embarrassed by a universal feature of human language.
edits.after: - "Sorry, what?" is a repair request.
edits.reason: Keep the function of the phrase without diagnosing the audience's emotional response.

edits.before: caption="Repair as a state machine. Most loops take one pass."
edits.after: caption="Repair as a state machine: initiate, repair, carry on."
edits.reason: Describe the diagram without an unsupported success-frequency claim.

edits.before: - The step people skip is the last one.
edits.after: - Point out the last step: accept the repair, then carry on.
edits.reason: Show the move to practise without asserting a typical omission.

edits.before: - Debrief on the ones that took more than one turn. Usually the mumble was at the start of the sentence.
edits.after: - Debrief on the ones that took more than one turn. Did the mumble's position make a difference?
edits.reason: Let the drill test an explanation instead of assigning it a customary result.

edits.before: It means the cheapest repair is the one that never needs you to speak. Which is why the 700 ms gap exists at all.
edits.after: Leaving a gap can give the speaker time to repair the problem without a prompt.
edits.reason: Keep one documented use of the gap without claiming it is the sole reason that gap exists.

edits.before: - Tie the three findings together here: self-repair preferred, initiations slow, delay makes room. They are one mechanism seen three ways.
edits.after: - Compare the three findings: who repairs the trouble, how long the gap is, and what the gap can allow.
edits.reason: Keep the synthesis while avoiding an untested assertion that the three findings establish one mechanism.

edits.before: The course's table, from the sources' findings. Read the right-hand column downwards.
edits.after: The course's proposed cost table. Test the turn counts in the repair drill.
edits.reason: Distinguish the proposed turn counts from the cited findings; the research notes do not establish these exact counts.

edits.before: - The last row is the one nobody teaches, and it is free.
edits.after: - The last row needs no spoken repair request; it still depends on the speaker noticing the trouble.
edits.reason: Keep what differs about silence without claiming nobody teaches it or that it guarantees a free repair.

edits.before: - So a fuller apology isn't a performance of sincerity. It does a job: it brings the anger down, and forgiveness follows that.
edits.after: - Keep the claim tied to the vignette scenarios and the reported role of anger reduction.
edits.reason: Match the lecture's removal of the sincerity claim and guaranteed progression to forgiveness.

edits.before: - Read the fourth one twice, then stop. The next slide is the course eating its own words.
edits.after: - Read the fourth one twice, then stop.
edits.reason: The next slide states the correction plainly; it does not need its own announcement.

edits.before: - Say it plainly. Do not soften it, and do not skip it --- a course that publishes errata in week 12 has to be able to do this in week 5.
edits.after: - State the correction before introducing the revised template.
edits.reason: Keep the teacher's instruction without another explanation of the course's consistency.

edits.before: - The explanation is now in, with two constraints that are the course's own and were the real objection all along.
edits.after: - The explanation is now in, with two constraints that are the course's own.
edits.reason: Keep ownership of the constraints without defending the earlier blanket exclusion.

edits.before: An explanation that arrives first, or runs long, is heard as an excuse --- which is a claim about how it lands, not about your honesty.
edits.after: An explanation that arrives first, or runs long, can be heard as an excuse.
edits.reason: Match the lecture's bounded description of a possible listener response.

edits.before: The situation beats the disposition. Which is to say: it's a protocol.
edits.after: The situation belongs in the bug report.
edits.reason: Match the lecture’s revised marginal joke and avoid turning explained variance into a definition.

edits.before: What you do and say after an error matters more than who the other person happens to be.
edits.after: Use the comparison as a reason to examine the situation, not to rank causes for a particular apology.
edits.reason: Keep the presenter’s practical application within the population-level result.

edits.before: - This is the evidence for the claim this week used to assert and couldn't support. Nobody has to be a naturally graceful apologiser.
edits.after: - Separate the association from a guarantee: an apology can matter without ensuring forgiveness.
edits.reason: Avoid repeating the course's correction history or converting a study association into a promise about every person.

edits.before: - Nobody reads the whole thing out. Say that twice --- the exercise fails if people write a safe one.
edits.after: - Say clearly that only the cost line is shared; nobody reads the whole apology out.
edits.reason: Keep the privacy condition without labelling students' protective responses a failed exercise.

edits.before: - Everyone assumes this one is a matter of character. It isn't. It's error handling, with a spec --- and now, with a meta-analysis.
edits.after: - Say both acceptance scripts aloud, including the option to ask for time.
edits.reason: End on usable choices rather than a universal claim about belief and another announcement of the course's evidence.

edits.before: - the **one-turn accept** --- the step people skip
edits.after: - the **one-turn accept** --- acknowledge the repair and carry on
edits.reason: Define the term by the action, without a prediction of failure.

edits.before: - Point at the glossary. Terms get introduced once and reused exactly; this is that promise being kept in public.
edits.after: - Point students to the three glossary entries.
edits.reason: Retain the navigation cue without praising the course for meeting its own promise.
